items.stem: You need the actual exception message text for a failing run. Which diagnostic script is the right starting point?

options.text: Starbridge-ExceptionRejections.sql
Starbridge-Deletions.sql
Starbridge-SerializedEntityData.sql
Starbridge-Cleanup.sql

items.explanation: ExceptionRejections joins Operation -> Message to surface the rejection/warning/exception text.

misconceptions.d: Cleanup mutates data — never reach for it just to read messages.

items.stem: A run fails with 'Synnduit.SynnduitException - An item with the same key has already been added.' Which script finds the cause, and what's the usual root cause?

options.text: Starbridge-CorruptionCheck.sql — it finds source IDs with more than one active mapping; the usual cause is two processes running against the same StarBridge database at once
Starbridge-ValueChange.sql — a field changed
Starbridge-Deletions.sql — records were deleted
Starbridge-Transactions.sql — just re-read the outcome counts

items.explanation: CorruptionCheck groups mappings and flags COUNT(*) > 1 (State <> 3) — duplicate active mappings, which throw the 'same key' exception. They typically come from concurrent processes against one StarBridge DB (the one-process rule, L1.5/L3.7); fix by restoring the most recent backup.

misconceptions.b: ValueChange shows field diffs, not duplicate mappings.
misconceptions.d: Transactions shows outcome counts; it won't surface the duplicate mappings behind the exception.

items.stem: In Starbridge-ExceptionRejections.sql, a Message Type of 3 means:

options.text: Rejection
Warning
Exception
Information

items.explanation: Type codes: 1 = Rejection, 2 = Warning, 3 = Exception, 4 = Information.

misconceptions.a: Rejection is Type 1; exceptions are Type 3.

items.stem: A teammate is about to run Starbridge-Cleanup.sql on production just to 'see what's failing'. What do you advise?
rubric: Cleanup-type scripts mutate data — they are not for read-only diagnosis
For 'what's failing' use a read-only script (ExceptionRejections / Transactions) instead
Read any script before running it; prefer read-only scripts on production
items.sampleAnswer: Don't — Cleanup mutates StarBridge data and isn't a diagnostic. To see what's failing, run a read-only script like ExceptionRejections (for the message text) or Transactions (for outcomes). Always read a script before running it, especially on production.
items.source: DiagnosticScripts/When and How to use these scripts.docx

items.stem: Where does the exception text live (not just the outcome), and how does ExceptionRejections.sql get it?
rubric: The text is in the Message table, linked to an Operation via OperationMessage
ExceptionRejections joins Operation -> OperationMessage -> Message (and out to EntityType / SourceSystemEntityId) and filters by Message Type
items.sampleAnswer: The message text is in the Message table, tied to an Operation through OperationMessage. ExceptionRejections does those joins (Operation -> OperationMessage -> Message, plus EntityType/SourceSystemEntityId) so you can read the exception/rejection text by Type.

items.stem: A transaction shows Outcome 6 (NotFoundInDestinationSystem): the source and its StarBridge mapping exist, but the destination record is gone, and you confirm the deletion was a mistake. How do you get the record back into the destination?

options.text: Set the mapping's State to 3 (Removed) — for the record and its child mappings, via [dbo].[SetMappingState] — so the next run treats it as brand new and re-inserts it
Just re-run the sync; it will automatically recreate the destination record
Delete the source record so both sides agree
Raise the garbage-collection threshold and re-run

items.explanation: Outcome 6 needs manual intervention. If the destination removal was a mistake, set State = 3 on the mapping and its children through [dbo].[SetMappingState] (not a raw UPDATE); with no active mapping, the record feeds through as an insert. (If the removal had been legitimate, you'd instead remove the source record.)

misconceptions.b: The engine takes no action on Outcome 6 — the mapping still points at a missing record, so a plain re-run just repeats the same outcome.
misconceptions.c: Removing the source is the fix when the removal was legitimate; here it was a mistake, so you restore the record instead.
misconceptions.d: Thresholds are unrelated to this manual fix.

items.stem: How does the support team learn about NotFoundInDestinationSystem and ReferredForManualDeduplication transactions across the CSSD syncs without running scripts by hand?

options.text: SynnduitEmailNotification queries each StarBridge DB for exceptions/rejections and the two manual-intervention outcomes, then emails the team a report
The Synnduit console prints them to a shared screen
They show up in the Windows Event Log automatically
There's no automation — someone runs the scripts on a schedule manually

items.explanation: SynnduitEmailNotification is a scheduled tool that monitors every sync's StarBridge DB for Exceptions/Rejections plus the two outcomes needing manual intervention (NotFoundInDestinationSystem and ReferredForManualDeduplication) and emails a report so support can work them.

misconceptions.d: That manual polling is exactly what SynnduitEmailNotification automates.
